🔥Day 15: The Spanish Empire – Gold, God, and Gunpowder🔥

🌎“The sun never set. And when it did, it bled gold.”🌍

They came from a fractured peninsula, kingdoms reborn from reconquest.

But once united under crown and faith, Spain became unstoppable.

It began with Columbus, but it was forged by Cortés, Pizarro, and legions of conquistadores.

From Tenochtitlán to Cuzco, empires older than Rome fell to steel, disease, and fire.

The Spanish Empire wasn’t just vast, it was everywhere.

From Manila to Mexico, Naples to New Granada.

It carried the cross, the Spanish tongue, and the Inquisition.

It claimed land, souls, and silver. 

Mountains were emptied. 

Kingdoms built from bullion.

But it also built cities, cathedrals, universities.

And while its glory glowed, it birthed rivals... England, Holland, France.

In time, the gold ran thin. 

The colonies rose.

But for centuries, Spain ruled not just with armies but with destiny, by the grace of God.

Because this empire didn’t just span the map.

It changed the map forever.

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) today conducted a site inspection at the MRT-7 Batasan Station along Commonwealth Avenue in Quezon City in a bid to address the recent flooding in the area, following President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s directive to ensure readiness this rainy season and strengthen disaster resilience. 

Based on the assessment conducted by the MMDA Flood Control and Sewerage Management Office, the ongoing construction of the MRT-7 contributed to the recent traffic congestion along Commonwealth Avenue brought about by heavy rains and floodings. The MRT-7 constructed a manhole directly above the existing drainage pipe culverts. A constructed footing wall of the ongoing MRT-7 construction was also observed, which may have partially obstructed the flow of water. It was also observed that access for regular maintenance of the drainage system is limited due to the presence of the MRT-7 project columns. Additionally, potholes and damaged drainage inlets were noted in the area.

Representatives from the Department of Transportation, Department of Public Works and Highways, Quezon City Government, and SMC MRT-7 Corporation also joined the inspection. 

#mmda #mmdaatyourservice
